offline_anchor_probe.scope: Offline mechanism probe on all 24 disclosed development tasks; zero model calls, no online or independent quality score.
offline_anchor_probe.anchors: Early first: first actual read response intersecting a compiler callable; most observed lines, then shortest span and lexical ID. Late same: same anchor with full native prefix. Late issue: rank all actually observed compiler callables by existing canonical code-tokenized BM25 over symbol identity and file, then the same deterministic ties; full native prefix.
offline_anchor_probe.annotation_use: Only after all anchors and all graph responses are fixed for each task. No annotation filtering or anchor retries.
offline_anchor_probe.interpretation: Deferring the same static anchor leaves annotated coverage absent from native unchanged at 80 lines; symbol/file BM25 ranking reduces it to 50. This does not establish a timing gain or an online quality gain. The subsequent model chooses a semantic relationship question, not a BM25-ranked anchor.

online_protocol.scope: Fresh three-arm development pilot, one previously disclosed task per language. Not independent validation or a leaderboard submission.
online_protocol.selection: First task of each language in the unchanged 24-task development selection order; no outcome-based substitution; no overlap with sealed 32.
online_protocol.graph_query_limit: Prompt limit of two calls per task, audited after the run; not a hard executor quota.
online_protocol.meter_guard: Observed SDK estimates, not invoiced charges. A final in-flight model turn may cross a guard; no retries or API fallback.
online_protocol.metrics: Official macro cumulative observed line Recall, precision and per-task F1 over all eight selected tasks. Missing and failed scores remain zero.
online_protocol.source_delivery: Only verified numbered source replies followed by an assistant response count as delivered. Graph novelty is measured against the prior candidate prefix and the complete matched native trajectory; annotations are used only after all outputs are frozen.
online_protocol.confounding: The primary contrast changes completion and graph use. The graph/functions contrast isolates graph availability and its prompt on the same prepared inputs; comparisons with older runs are descriptive only.
online_protocol.policy_changes_after_start: None. Freeze runtime, prompts, source, graphs and analysis before inference. Retain first attempts and every selected task; no gold source or reference patch enters prompts.
online_protocol.passing_scope: Development selection only. A new independent protocol and broader native solver coverage are still required before the official 500.

online_gate.diagnostic_correction: Overlap counts corrected after frozen analysis using official path normalization. Original protocol, scores and first gate file remain unchanged; this amendment does not relax a gate.

posthoc_clangd_range_diagnostic.scope: Post-hoc zero-model mechanism diagnosis on disclosed development tasks. Fixed queries and original preceding messages; not a new online outcome or a counterfactual agent.
posthoc_clangd_range_diagnostic.repair: Choose the smallest containing tree-sitter span when materializing clangd definitions. Preserve compiler selection, symbol identity and every edge. Missing chunks retain point definitions.

javascript.decision: Provider emits assigned property names only as local references without a callable definition/enclosing range. Do not invent compiler-defined callables or calls. Chunker assignment support already exists.

posthoc_clangd_range_diagnostic.outcome: 38 ranges shrink across three C++ graphs, with identical compiler identities, selection points and edges. The changed late C++ query selects the observed constructor instead of rgb; it has no returned neighbors. No query gains physical or annotated source. Eight of nine replies stay identical. No online quality claim, relaxed gate, or full-500 launch.
posthoc_clangd_range_diagnostic.limits: Smallest containing parsed span does not repair every macro parse error. JavaScript callable definition coverage and useful multi-language graph delivery remain open. Prior failed gates and official scores stay unchanged.

posthoc_commonjs_diagnostic.scope: Post-hoc compiler-only diagnosis on a disclosed JavaScript development task. A complete existing LSP route and original fixed-query replay, not a new online outcome or a backend promotion.

synthetic.interpretation: Assigned exports/module/alias functions lack callable definitions under all three configurations. Function declarations and classes work. Variable-held arrows have enclosing source but are classified as fields; that separate SCIP decoder issue remains open.

repair.consumer: Existing shared LSP client, generic LSP graph route and TypeScript incremental patching
repair.rule: Use advertised TypeScript navtree only for callable symbols with whole-body fallback selections. Recover one compiler name span with the exact same name/body; retain originals for missing, stale or ambiguous compiler evidence.

full_graph.preparation: Private clean clone; allowJs tsconfig lists exactly the prior SCIP document inventory, including tests. No dependencies installed; generated config removed before clone audit.

posthoc_commonjs_diagnostic.open_gate: Establish useful relationship queries and multi-language delivery before a newly frozen matched candidate. Active SCIP assigned-function coverage, broader repository validation and downstream repair effects remain open.

posthoc_source_gap_diagnostic.scope: Fixed-trajectory source gap decomposition, preserving official annotation paths and counts. Missing source locations are reported separately; suffix candidates never receive read credit.
posthoc_source_gap_diagnostic.normalizer_example: The pinned official normalizer strips leading dots from .github/.golangci/.goreleaser paths. These paths and score denominators remain untouched; unavailable source is reported as evaluation-only metadata.
posthoc_source_gap_diagnostic.initial_attempt: Source observations and completion sets were frozen for all 72 records, then the first analysis stopped because it assumed every canonical annotation file existed. The separate v2 analysis preserves that failure and classifies missing source locations explicitly.
posthoc_source_gap_diagnostic.limits: Pooled physical-line counts, including blank/comment lines, are not macro averages. Out-of-range means beyond the source reader splitlines count; 11 of the 28 such lines are the single position after a file terminates. No paths are remapped and no annotation lines are removed.

bounded_file_remainder_replay.scope: Fixed-trajectory feasibility only, not a new online outcome.
bounded_file_remainder_replay.policy: Preserve original function-completed replies, then add an entire unseen remainder only for a file touched by the current original read/content-grep reply and only within the same total 2048-token completion budget and output limit. Files are at most 1500 lines and 2 MB; no annotation or issue-based selection.
bounded_file_remainder_replay.control: 234 first-source and 76 late-pilot source replies reproduce exactly. All 32 original trajectory predictions reproduce exactly; eight tasks repeat from the 24 and are not independent.
bounded_file_remainder_replay.decision: Rejected before product implementation or model inference: F1 falls in both fixed-trajectory cohorts despite Recall gains and annotated additions across three languages. Do not substitute these arithmetic replay results for new online evidence.
bounded_file_remainder_replay.next: Prioritize relationship selection and source attribution from actual solver/test feedback; preserve all failed gates and sealed independent tasks. No official-500 launch.
